result.rationale: Verifiable from the diff: Post#cook returns `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the cooking/sanitization pipeline. TopicEmbed.import passes external RSS/scraped content as raw with cook_method raw_html (skip_validations: true), and embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Imported external HTML, including any script tags from the polled feed or scraped page, is stored and rendered verbatim — a stored XSS vector against embed visitors. This is a genuine security defect introduced by the diff.

judged_text: Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim for cook_method raw_html, and TopicEmbed.import feeds unsanitized external RSS/scraped HTML through this path, so the entire sanitization pipeline is bypassed for imported content. Any HTML/JS in a polled feed or scraped page is stored as-is in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb (and on the main forum topic), giving an external feed author stored XSS against every visitor of the embed page; the imported-content trust boundary is inverted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating posts and feeds it external HTML (`contents` from RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse` and from scraping via `Readability::Document#content`) with no sanitization shown in the diff. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, making stored XSS from untrusted feed/page content a verifiable risk introduced by this change.
